gg1.same_expectation_why: Thirteen of these sit top-left on a panel or page and close it; the three on the incognito screen sit top-right in place of the ghost, so I think they switch a mode off rather than close a panel.
gg1.affects_navigation: Yes. I would learn 'X in the top-left closes the thing I opened' and then find an X in the opposite corner that ends incognito instead; I would hesitate before pressing any X in case it throws away the chat I am in.

first_pass.why: The same X is used for two jobs (close a panel, leave incognito) and it is not even in the same corner, so I cannot rely on either its position or its picture; nothing written tells me which job the top-right one does.
first_pass.solution: Keep the close X in one position (top-left) everywhere. On the incognito screen replace the X with a text button that says 'Leave incognito' or 'Exit incognito chat'.

test_cases.what_to_try: Open the app on your phone. Press the ghost in the top-right corner of the chat screen. Then press the X that is now in that top-right corner, and tell me whether what happened is what you told me it would do.
test_cases.real_if: you end up somewhere you did not predict, or you cannot tell afterwards what the X did
test_cases.not_real_if: you land where you predicted and can tell what the X did
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the app on the chat screen with the ghost top-right. I pressed the ghost. The screen changed to 'Incognito chat' and the ghost was replaced by an X in the same corner. The keyboard also opened by itself, which I had not asked for. I pressed the X. The 'Incognito chat' title went away, the normal greeting came back, and the ghost was back in the corner. That is exactly what I predicted: the top-right X ends incognito and returns me to the normal chat. I could tell what it did because the title disappeared and the ghost returned. I finished it. Note: the phone was slow, and some screenshots showed the screen from one step earlier, so I took two after each press to be sure.

test_cases.what_to_try: From the chat screen, press the + at the bottom left to open the panel, then press the X at the top left of that panel. Compare what this X did with what the top-right X did.
test_cases.real_if: the two X marks do things you would not have expected to share one picture, and nothing on screen told you in advance
test_cases.not_real_if: both did what you expected from them
test_cases.what_happened: I was in the incognito chat when I pressed the +. The 'Add to chat' panel came up from the bottom with its X in the top-left. The incognito X was still visible top-right, dimmed behind it, so there were two identical X marks on one screen. I pressed the panel's X. Only the panel closed and I stayed in the incognito chat. So the two X marks did two different jobs, close this panel versus leave incognito, and each did what I had predicted. Nothing written on screen said which was which. I relied on position, the top-left X sitting on the panel and the top-right one under the 'Incognito chat' title, and it held. I finished it.

test_cases.what_happened: I was in an incognito chat. I opened the side menu with the three lines and pressed the large word 'Claude' at the top. The menu closed, I was taken OUT of incognito into a new empty normal chat (ghost back top-right, normal greeting), and the keyboard opened by itself. I expected nothing to happen, because it looks like a heading. Instead it changed my chat and my mode. Then I opened the menu again and pressed '+ New chat'. The result was the same: the menu closed, a new empty chat, keyboard open. So the heading is a hidden second 'New chat' button, and it left incognito without warning. I finished it, and afterwards I pressed Back once to close the keyboard. I typed nothing.
